content.title: About
content.content: Chicken nuggets are small pieces of chicken breast that are breaded and fried or baked. They are a popular fast‑food snack and are often served with a variety of dipping sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Nuggets were first introduced in the United States in the 1970s as part of fast‑food menus.
Traditional breading consists of flour, spices and breadcrumbs, but modern versions may use cornflakes or nut mixes.
Nuggets are frequently included in kids' meals because they are easy to eat with small hands.
There is a “golden” nugget version where the coating is tinted with edible gold for special occasions.
Some countries have introduced limits on salt and fat content in nuggets to improve their nutritional profile.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Chicken meat is rich in complete protein, essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Nuggets contain niacin, vitamin B6 and B12, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Chicken provides iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for blood formation and bone health.

items.title: Low in carbs
items.content: When consumed in moderation, nuggets fit into low‑carbohydrate diets.

items.title: Taste appeal
items.content: The crispy coating makes the product appealing to both children and adults, encouraging a more varied diet.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Fried nuggets can be calorie‑dense and contain saturated fats, so they should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: The breading often contains a lot of salt, which may raise blood pressure in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Breadings may include gluten, dairy or eggs, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: Cooking in certain oils can produce trans fats, which are detrimental to cardiovascular health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Nuggets are usually served hot with sauces such as ketchup, mayo, barbecue or honey‑mustard. They are convenient to eat with hands and can be added to salads, wraps, or used as a topping on pizza.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked nuggets in the refrigerator in an airtight container for up to 2‑3 days. Frozen nuggets keep for up to 3 months; reheat them to an internal temperature of 75 °C before consumption.
